##

# Vocabulary

A name can move behind an alias; a VALUE cannot. `sourceType` is one field with
one string in it, and a client sw

itching on `"scenario"` has no second name to
fall back to. So the values negotiate.

Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and t

he renamed values read canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Vocabulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario`
| `study` |\n| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun` | `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioI
d`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRefId` |\n| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `sce

nario` | `study` |
| trace-destination `sourceTypes` | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today's
contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spell
ing; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one, because\na boundary that accepts a spelling it does not announce is one t

wo
implementations can disagree about. A response that varies by vocabulary sends
`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary`.

This is a
**separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is\neval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedule. A deployment may

speak one
and not the other, so read
`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` — `apiVocabulary` and `vocabulary` are
two block
s — before sending either. With the SDK:\n`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or\n`client.withApiVocabulary(2)` on o

ne you already hold.

Permalink resource types are the exception that proves the rule: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical
keys, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\n
OPERATION rather than the header — a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.

apiVocabulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.

### Browser tools on chat sessions

> [!NOTE]
>
> Hosted browser availability dep
ends on the account and deployment. The browser workspace must be enabled to open the live pane in the Playground.\n\n`POST /chat-
sessions/messages` accepts an optional `browser: { policy?, profileId? }`. Attach it on every turn that should browse. The initial
grant and profile are fixed; the current host policy and pinned read-only mode can narrow the effective permissions. Responses an
d traces include the read-only `chatSessionId`, browser metadata, and screenshot URLs without inline image data.\n\n| Method | Pat
h | Purpose |\n| - | - | - |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/browser` | Create an empty API session and its browser with `projectId`, `p
olicy`, optional `profileId`, and a stable `idempotencyKey`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/open` | Open or wake
the session browser. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/command` | Execute a browser command under the session policy
with a stable `commandId`. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/note` | Append a command-ledger note. |\n| POST | `/ch
at-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/trace` | Read command receipts and screenshot evidence. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/br
owser/artifact` | Resolve a command screenshot URL. |\n| POST | `/chat-sessions/{sessionId}/browser/close` | Release the session d
esktop. |\n\nOnly the owning user can drive an API session's browser. All inputs use the public `sessionId`; conversation and brow
ser identifiers in responses are informational. Capacity refusals before execution release the turn lease so the same idempotency

key can be retried. An execution with an unknown outcome must be inspected before attempting a new action.

# CLI Overview

> Local MCP testing and mcpjam cloud: probing, debugging, OAuth, conformance, and hosted evals fr
om your terminal\n\nThe `mcpjam` CLI is two invocations. Local MCP testing stays at the top level: inspect, debug, and test MCP se
rvers from the command line or CI (connectivity, OAuth, MCP Apps, tools/resources/prompts, protocol conformance). Most local comma
nds are one-shot; `mcpjam mcp` and `subscriptions listen` keep a process open. Account-bound commands live under `mcpjam cloud` an
d talk to your MCPJam account. There are no compatibility aliases for the old Cloud paths — see [Migrating to CLI 4.0](https://doc

s.mcpjam.com/cli/migration.md).

## Recommended: Use with Agent Skills

The easiest way to use the CLI is through the [MCPJam
skill](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/tree/main/skills/mcp-inspector), which gives your agent full context on every command a

nd workflow.

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
npx skills add mcpjam/inspector --skill mcp-inspector
```

To conv
ert existing promptfoo, pytest, Jest, or CSV tests, use the [MCP eval import skill](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/tree/main/

port
```

To drive MCPJam's hosted eval tools — launch a run, poll it to a verdict, and triage a failure down to the step — use
the [run MCPJam evals skill](https://github.com/MCPJam/inspector/tree/main/skills/run-mcpjam-evals). This one is about running su

run-mcpjam-evals
```

Once installed, your agent will know how and when to invoke `mcpjam` commands automatically.

## Insta

ll

```bash theme={"theme":"css-variables"}
# Global (gives you the mcpjam command)
npm i -g @mcpjam/cli

# Or run witho

ut installing
npx -y @mcpjam/cli@latest --help
```

> [!NOTE]
>
> All examples in these docs use `mcpjam` directly. If you i

nstalled via `npx`,
> replace `mcpjam` with `npx -y @mcpjam/cli@latest`.
